notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Uploads from the web page: when an upload stops moving, because the phone's screen locked or the WiFi dropped, the page now tries again by itself. If it still cannot go on, it says the upload stopped and why that usually happens, with Try again, which picks up where it stopped. Every upload is written to a log on the console, and the debug report includes it, so a stuck upload can be traced.

Handheld, only the power button wakes the console. A button press or a touch no longer lights the screen after it turns itself off, or wakes the console from the power button's sleep, so a console in its case stays asleep. Docked, a controller still wakes it, since the power button can be out of reach.

Cheats on the web page: add many at once. In the Cheats section, pick the game, choose A list of cheats, then paste a list from a cheat site or choose a cheat file (.txt, .ini, .cht or .pnach). The page shows what it found before adding anything and skips codes the game already has. They are added switched off; turn them on from the game's Cheats menu. This works for GameCube and Wii, DS, PS2 and the RetroArch systems.

Stremio plays video on the console's hardware decoder, which uses about a third of the processor it took before. If a stream misbehaves, turn off Hardware video decoding in Stremio's menu.

PlayStation games on PCSX ReARMed can render at twice the resolution: set Internal resolution to 2x in the game's menu. Original stays the default.

Standalone PPSSPP: Fast-forward from the pause menu works. It did nothing before.

PC games: a disc image over 4 GB can be added now. It goes to the Linux partition and is unpacked there, since the SD card cannot hold a file that big.

Manage Files lists 3DS and Wii U saves by the game's name instead of a code, and 3DS save states show their slot.

A Wii U disc image uploaded together with its .key is no longer flagged as a duplicate and skipped.

New and lightly tested: the upload retries were checked by cutting the connection on purpose, not yet with a phone locking mid-upload. Waking with a controller while docked was not checked with a dock. Stremio's hardware decoding was checked with test streams, not Plex yet. The big PC disc was a test disc, not a real game's installer. 3DS save names were checked with .3ds and .cci games, Wii U with a .wux.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
